summary: Fix: train tip (Friday = 6 per Wikipedia, plus bus not on Sundays/public holidays), Putangirua bio 'head of valley', Southern Crossing length hedge, Tararua park bio (drop unverified 1,571 m), Cobblestones holiday closures, Holdsworth ticketUrl preference. All 15 proposed ticketUrls loaded with 200 and titles naming the place. Both coordinate proposals are source-backed but audit-spot-coordinates.ts not run. Not verified: live Metlink timetable (JS-only page), Cape Palliser hours, Pūkaha talk times beyond 2026-10-17.

items.note: Variant 1. Location, pinot noir and Cape Palliser all sourced (Wikivoyage, Wikipedia).

Variant 1. Day-trippers, shelter from westerlies, warm dry climate, Martinborough wine, pinot noir + sauvignon blanc, Masterton largest town (Wikipedia: ~22,600), 'over 1000' commuters all match Wikivoyage Wairarapa / Wikipedia. Minor: 'strung along the way' for Carterton, Greytown, Featherston is loose (Wikivoyage's city list omits Greytown) but true on SH2/the rail line.

Variant 1. Paths of the Dead filming (Wikipedia; DOC says Dimholt Road/Army of the Dead scenes in Return of the King), Cape Palliser lighthouse at southern tip (Wikivoyage), kiwi/kākā/takahē at Pūkaha (operator wildlife list). Photo for slot 3 is Lens's job.
Variant 1 matches whyVisit variant 1.

Frequencies are NOT uniform on weekdays. Wikipedia 'Wairarapa Connection' infobox/text: Mon-Thu five each way, Friday six each way (extra Friday-night service), Sat/Sun/public holidays two each way. Wikivoyage Wairarapa says '5 weekday / 2 weekend' (matches draft) but Wikivoyage Martinborough says six trains/day. 91 km confirmed (Wikipedia). Live Metlink timetable did not load (JS-only), so the Friday figure is unconfirmed against today's timetable. Bus 200: Wikivoyage Martinborough (5 times/day from Masterton and Featherston) but Wikivoyage Wairarapa says buses do not run Sundays or public holidays; the tip omits that and should include it.

corrected.title: Trains stop at Masterton
corrected.detail: The Wairarapa Line runs 91 km from Wellington to Masterton, with five services each way on weekdays (a sixth on Friday evenings) but only two at weekends and on public holidays. There is no train to Martinborough; Metlink bus 200 runs there from Masterton and Featherston, but not on Sundays or public holidays.

items.note: Reloaded Wikivoyage Wairarapa Wine section: 'Martinborough Wine Centre ... Cycle hire is available for $40 per day (bookings essential)'. Hours Daily 10-17 (winter), Fri/Sat to 19:00 (summer). Vineyard layout: Wikipedia Martinborough: 'Almost all the vineyards are in thin ribbons around the northern and eastern sides of the town, and on the Dry River to the south'. Tip wording is supported. Listing is undated, so do not add the $40 price; optionally add 'bookings essential'.
DOC media release (2021, loaded): 'sharp teeth and can move quickly if they feel threatened... at least 20 metres'; keep dogs on a leash and away; do not get between seal and sea.
Variant 1: Union Jack plan and 1879 (Wikivoyage; Wikipedia says 'Union Flag', 'in the 19th century'), vineyards in ribbons north and east (Wikipedia).
'Cellar door hours vary' is a safe qualifier; old 11-5 unsourced.
Removal of 10-20 NZD justified (no source). Optional free:true is owner's call.

'at the head of the Pūtangirua Stream valley' is not in DOC or Wikipedia (Wikipedia only has 'gorge below the pinnacles'). Everything else holds: lookout on Pinnacles Ridge Track is DOC's recommended view; Paths of the Dead filming is Wikipedia (DOC says Dimholt Road scenes in Return of the King).
items.corrected: Eroded gravel pillars cut by the Pūtangirua Stream, seen best from the Pinnacles Ridge Track lookout and filmed as the Paths of the Dead in The Lord of the Rings.

DOC page states 'GPS coordinates -41.449483, 175.221505' and 'parking, a toilet, a shelter and a campsite near the reserve entrance', so the proposal is the car park/reserve entrance, matching WRITING.md. Stored -41.4468,175.2468 equals Wikipedia's formation point (-41.4467,175.2467), about 2.1 km east. Still run audit-spot-coordinates.ts (this was not run). If the owner wants the pin on the formation, keep the stored value.

Variant 1: reef, lagoon, lighthouse, 162 m Castle Rock, daisy found only here, all on DOC page. 'beneath' Castle Rock for the lighthouse is loose but fine.

nature is reasonable (owner's call).

Variant 1: first Arbor Day celebration in NZ held in Greytown on 3 July 1890; tree register kept; on SH2 (Wikipedia). Variant 2/3 facts also hold: settled 27 March 1854 under Small Farms Association scheme, named for Sir George Grey, 24 km SW of Masterton. Note for the flag: Wikipedia (citing Te Ara) does say the main street has boutique, antique stores and cafés, and Greytown won NZ's Most Beautiful Small Town 2017; the stored 'Victorian shopfronts' wording is still unsourced. Counted-source question remains open for the owner.

Variant 1: Wikipedia 'open-sky observatory inspired by and built on a similar scale to the famous Stonehenge'; operator references Southern Hemisphere night sky. Cutting 'Phoenix Astronomical Society' was unnecessary: Wikipedia does say the society (TPAS) organised construction, completed 2005 (opened 12 Feb 2005). Optional.
Operator homepage: self-guided open daily 10 AM-4 PM; guided tours 10:30am, 12:30pm, 2pm.
Operator: self-guided $5-$18. Draft range matches.
Loads (200); title 'Stonehenge Aotearoa | New Zealand's Astronomical Henge & Star Compass'.

Variant 1 confirmed against DOC pages I loaded: Holdsworth Lodge sleeps 28 and is bookable; Atiwhakatu Track starts from Mt Holdsworth Road car park and passes Donnelly Flat picnic/camping; Masterton 17 km from Holdsworth (Tararua page); Jumbo Circuit 24 km loop, 2-3 days. (Research said these pages were not loaded; they are fine.)

Proposed URL loads (200, 'Tararua Forest Park: Wairarapa places to visit') but a more specific official page exists and loads: Holdsworth Lodge page. Prefer it, or keep the park page if the owner wants both Holdsworth and the standalone park to share one.

-40.9064,175.4767 is within about 50 m of Wikivoyage's Mt Holdsworth-Jumbo Circuit start (-40.9061,175.4764), which DOC describes as starting at the Holdsworth road end by the lodge. The true car park lies a little beyond the lodge (DOC Atiwhakatu: car park at end of Mt Holdsworth Road, past the lodge), so expect <=~300 m offset: acceptable at the ~100 m guide only if the audit agrees. Stored point is 4.4 km away; moving it is right.

Hours right but operator's page is now fully readable: open daily; Jun-Aug 10am-3pm (last admission 2:30), Sep-May 10am-4pm (last admission 3:30). Route Ōtaki Forks - Mount Hector - Kaitoke confirmed (DOC, Wikipedia); one of four classic tramps; Middle Crossing (Ōtaki Forks to Holdsworth, 4 days) confirmed. '32 km' is Wikipedia's figure but DOC's leg distances total 34.5 km (5+5+7.5+17); DOC says 3 days, Wikipedia 2-3 days. Use a hedged figure. 'For experienced trampers only': DOC grades it 'Advanced tramping track' and says tops routes are for experienced trampers; ok.
items.corrected: An alpine tramp of about 32 km and two to three days from Ōtaki Forks over Mount Hector to Kaitoke, one of the Tararua Range's four classic tramps and graded advanced by DOC.

items.note: DOC leg times: 3-4, 3-4, 5-6, 8-9 h = 19-23 h walking. Correct sum.
